title: Optimal measurements and near-linear decoding for universal ℓ₂/ℓ₁ sparse recovery
formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(C,B>0\), \(a\geq0\), and a deterministic recovery scheme such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(1\leq k\leq n\), one fixed matrix \(A_{n,k}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\leq Bk\log_2(en/k)\) permits recovery from \(A_{n,k}x\) in at most \(Bn\log_2^a(n+2)\) operations, with \[\|x-\widehat x\|_2\leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{k}}\min_{z:\,|\operatorname{supp}(z)|\leq k}\|x-z\|_1\] simultaneously for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\)?
why: The target combines information-efficient sensing with fast, uniformly reliable reconstruction for arbitrary signals. Resolving it would show whether the strongest standard universal mixed-norm guarantee can be obtained without sacrificing near-optimal compression or practical asymptotic decoding time.
status_note: The 2009 source poses this universal mixed-norm tradeoff, and the checked later for-all recovery paper still distinguishes it from its ℓ₁/ℓ₁ result. No matching resolution was located in the bounded September 2026 check. The arithmetic/preprocessing convention is explicit; efficient explicit matrix generation is not asserted to be part of the original target.

importance.reason: A central universal compressed-sensing tradeoff between measurement count, robust mixed-norm error and decoding time; explicit matrix generation is a separate issue.

sentences: A fixed matrix compresses every real signal to a short vector of linear measurements.
The decoder must work for all signals with error controlled by the best k-sparse ℓ₁ tail divided by √k.
The conjecture combines O(k log(en/k)) measurements with near-linear deterministic decoding.
The arithmetic model permits input-independent polynomial preprocessing but charges decoding accesses.
Faster results with an ℓ₁ reconstruction error or only per-input randomized success do not meet this target.

definitions: The support of a vector is the set of its nonzero coordinates; a vector is \(k\)-sparse if its support has size at most \(k\). The norms are \(\|v\|_1=\sum_i|v_i|\) and \(\|v\|_2=(\sum_i v_i^2)^{1/2}\). The minimum in the statement is the sum of absolute values outside the \(k\) largest-magnitude coordinates of \(x\); ties may be broken arbitrarily. The decoder receives \(n,k\), the exact real measurement vector \(y=A_{n,k}x\), and read-only access to the fixed description of the scheme. It receives neither \(x\) nor its support, and must output all \(n\) coordinates of \(\widehat x\). The output need not itself be sparse. Measurements are linear and selected independently of the unknown signal. We use the real-arithmetic model: real addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero number, square root of a nonnegative number, comparison, and access to an addressed stored entry each cost one operation; ordinary integer index operations cost one as well. The decoder is one fixed algorithm, with polynomial-size read-only advice depending only on \(n,k\), including the matrix and any preprocessing data. Reading advice is charged. Advice generation and forming the original measurement vector are outside the requested decoding bound. No polynomial-time explicit matrix construction is required. Once the scheme is fixed its decoder is deterministic and the guarantee holds for all real signals; a matrix chosen by the probabilistic method is admissible only if a single fixed choice works for all signals. Constants, the polynomial advice exponent and the decoding exponent are independent of \(n,k,x\). Measurements are noiseless; no additional post-measurement perturbation is included.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction or existence proof of a scheme meeting both resource bounds and the universal mixed-norm error guarantee in the specified arithmetic model, or prove that no such scheme exists. A guarantee holding with high probability separately for each input, an ℓ₁/ℓ₁ error bound, or optimal row count with slower decoding is insufficient.

context_blocks.text: The source’s “deterministic” target is universal recovery from one matrix: the same measurements must work for every signal. Editorial model convention: this card makes the arithmetic-operation and preprocessing conventions explicit, without adding the separate challenge of efficient deterministic matrix generation. It also uses \(\log(en/k)\) and \(k\geq1\) to remove the source formula’s undefined or zero endpoint expressions.

For exactly \(k\)-sparse signals the right-hand side is zero, so the scheme must recover them exactly. For nonsparse signals, recovery quality depends on the entire tail and gains a factor \(1/\sqrt{k}\). Merely outputting a plausible support does not establish this robust guarantee.

The original question emphasizes achieving optimal measurement count and fast reconstruction together. Classical constructions achieve the two features separately for this error criterion, whereas some fast optimal-measurement schemes use a different norm on the reconstruction error.

The later for-all sparse-recovery work of Gilbert, Li, Porat and Strauss improves measurements and decoding for the ℓ₁/ℓ₁ formulation, and explicitly lists mixed-norm recovery as a remaining direction. Its use of a matrix fixed for all signals is compatible with a nonconstructive probabilistic existence proof.

The inequality \(\|v\|_2\leq\|v\|_1\) does not convert an \(\ell_1/\ell_1\) theorem into the requested result: it loses the essential \(1/\sqrt{k}\) factor. Likewise, an input-dependent success probability does not imply that one random seed works simultaneously over the uncountable set of all real inputs.

When \(k\) is comparable to \(n\), storing the full vector is consistent with the measurement bound. The compression challenge lies in the sparse regime. Counting the output cost explains why near-linear decoding remains a meaningful target even when the number of measurements is much smaller than \(n\).
